newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher, edge up in early trade.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher, edge up in early trade.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened higher on Tuesday and edged up a bit further in early trade.
Short-covering overnight in overseas trade and firm European debt markets was a positive influence, analysts said. Ten-year maturities attracted some buyers.

A rumored 0.5 percent decline in the BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index for the week ended August 9 might also have contributed to the early firmness in New York, analysts said. The index rose 0.5 percent a week earlier.
In early trade, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 9/32 to 96-27/32, yielding 6.62 percent.
Besides the BTM/Shroder weekly store sales report, the market gets a report at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT on second-quarter productivity and unit labor costs.
Economists polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that productivity rose 0.7 percent during the second quarter and that unit labor costs rose 2.7 percent.
Two regional Federal Reserve bank surveys are also due -- the Atlanta Federal Reserve Bank index at 0900 EDT/1300 GMt and the Richmond Fed survey at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
